senses.sense_definition: The quality of being careful and sensible; good judgment in practical matters to avoid mistakes or risks.

examples.text: Financial <w>prudence</w> dictates that we save at least three months of living expenses for unexpected emergencies.
The committee decided that <w>prudence</w> was necessary before investing such a large sum of public money.

senses.sense_definition: Careful management of money and resources to avoid unnecessary waste; thrift.

examples.text: Through years of strict <w>prudence</w>, the family managed to pay off their mortgage much earlier than anticipated.
Her natural <w>prudence</w> prevented her from spending money on items that were not strictly essential.

senses.sense_definition: Careful preparation for the future, characterized by foresight and provision.

examples.text: With admirable <w>prudence</w>, the captain checked the changing weather forecasts before guiding the vessel out to sea.
They lacked the <w>prudence</w> to plan for the upcoming winter, which left them vulnerable when supplies ran low.

senses.sense_definition: Wisdom and deep understanding applied to moral conduct and practical decision-making.

examples.text: Ancient philosophers often regarded <w>prudence</w> as the cardinal virtue guiding all moral action.
The elderly leader spoke with profound <w>prudence</w>, calming the anxious crowd with measured words.

senses.sense_definition: A female given name, originally popular as a Puritan virtue name.

examples.text: <w>Prudence</w> greeted the guests warmly as soon as they walked through the front door.
Her grandmother was named <w>Prudence</w>, following a long-standing family naming tradition.
